❈ On 21 October, the Orthodox Church celebrates the Holy Transylvanian Confessors.

• Over the centuries, the Orthodox Church of Transylvania was a martyr Church. Countless were the wrongs done by the 18th-century masters of Transylvania to the Transylvanian Church, including its servants and its faithful. But many too were those who fought to defend the Orthodox faith of their forefathers against the oppression of the imperial power in Vienna.

• Six holy Transylvanian confessors – two priests, two monks and two free peasants, martyrs of the true faith of their forefathers – in an icon painted on glass. Saints in whom the whole Orthodox Church of Transylvania is embodied: hierarchs and clergy, monks and hermits, the multitude of the faithful.

• These fighters were: Oprea Miclăuș (a peasant from Săliște, near Sibiu), who suffered death for the true faith; the hieromonks Visarion Sarai and Sofronie of Cioara (near Orăștie); the priests Moise Măcinic of Sibiel and Ioan of Galeș (all five celebrated on 21 October); and Atanasie Todoran of Bichigiu, Bistrița-Năsăud (celebrated on 12 November).

• The icon was painted to order, so it is not available. It can be made again, to order.

ff82a1798fc9:
▫︎ For Orthodox Christians, the feast of Pentecost is not just the memory of a historical event. It is a celebration of the faithful's belonging to the Church. They have lived the Descent of the Holy Spirit and received “the seal of the gift of the Holy Spirit” through the sacrament of anointing with Holy Chrism.

▫︎“Fifty days after the Resurrection of the Lord, at the Jewish feast called Pentecost (fifty days after the feast of the Exodus), while the Apostles and other disciples of the Lord Jesus Christ were gathered together in prayer in the "upper room", the Holy Spirit came down upon them in the form of “divided tongues of fire”, with the sound of a mighty wind, and they began to speak in languages they did not know. At that time there were many pilgrims in Jerusalem from the Jewish diaspora, come for the feast, who were greatly amazed to hear these unschooled fishermen saying prayers to the Lord in the languages of their distant countries.” (This event is described in detail in the Acts of the Apostles, chapter 2)

▫︎ The number fifty, from the fifty days after the Resurrection, bears witness to eternal and heavenly fullness, being seven times seven, plus one.

▫︎ The icon of the Descent of the Holy Spirit (model: Nicula, 19th century) is especially beautiful, because I painted it on anti-reflective glass.

Every year on 14 September, the Orthodox Church celebrates «the Exaltation of the Holy Cross»

“Whenever we go through suffering, trouble or illness, if we make the sign of the Holy Cross, think of the Saviour Jesus Christ and ask for help, then He, with His merciful love, turns physical suffering into spiritual victory and gives us strength to carry the cross of our life.” (Patriarch Daniel)

The icon I am showing you today, on the day of the great feast of «the Exaltation of the Holy Cross», depicts «Saints Constantine and Helen, the Emperors», in the traditional model of the two emperors standing on either side of the Holy Cross.

“... The emperor saw the cross in the sky, and the empress found the cross of Christ in the earth. That is why, in the icon of the saints, the cross that joins heaven and earth stands between them. The holy Emperors hold the cross between them as the mystery of the boundless love of Christ, crucified, risen and ascended in glory. So the holy Emperors Constantine and Helen are bound to the Mystery of the Holy Cross because they felt the power of Christ, the power of Christ's resurrection hidden mysteriously in His sacrificial, humble and merciful love...” (the Patriarch of Romania).

The icon I am showing you today is not available; a few days ago it arrived in its little home, where it was awaited with the joy of standing beside two other icons painted in our workshop.

bf293f999341:
• Saint Charalambos the Hieromartyr (10 February)

• On 10 February, the Romanian Orthodox Church celebrates Saint Charalambos, protector of the poor and the sick and deliverer from plague. A saint to whom the Romanian peasant (especially in 18th–19th century Transylvania) once prayed for protection from plague, cholera, typhoid fever and the other epidemics that used to ravage people. The same Romanian peasant “painted” Saint Charalambos in countless icons on glass. One of them (painted in a Transylvanian workshop in the early 19th century) is the model of the icon I am showing you today, an icon painted in our workshop.

• The icon shows Saint Charalambos binding the plague, and so saving the city. Charalambos is shown in the usual way, dressed in robe, mantle and omophorion, with the holy book and halo, giving a blessing; he tramples the plague, which is bound by a chain. The plague, carrying a scythe, has the face of a horned man.

a9a9e0e4e3bb:
⊹10 February: «Saint Charalambos enthroned, binding the plague»

• Model: Transylvanian workshop, Laz, first half of the 19th century

• The saint is shown seated on a bishop's throne, symbolising his spiritual power and his victory over death. Under the saint's feet or beside the throne there is always a demonic figure, often winged, carrying a scythe.

• This scene reflects the popular devotion to the saint who delivered whole communities from devastating epidemics, such as the famous «Caragea's plague» in Bucharest.

• These icons were not only objects of worship; they also had a strong protective (apotropaic) role, guarding the home and the family against contagious diseases.

• Icons showing Saint Charalambos in this form are considered collector's pieces.

ee104841166b:
«Saint Charalambos enthroned, binding the plague» – a study after an icon made in a Transylvanian workshop in the early 19th century.

The Akathist to the Saint says: "Rejoice, deliverer from plague and famine!"

It happened in Wallachia. In 1813, more than 300 people died in Bucharest every day, when "Caragea's plague" swept away more than 90,000 people.

The Romanians' only salvation was Saint Charalambos, known in the tradition of the Romanian people as the deliverer from the plague epidemic, to whom prayers for salvation were raised day and night.

The central scene of the icon recreates the moment when Saint Charalambos binds the neck of the figure of the plague with a heavy iron chain, so that it can no longer harm people.
